newsitem.title: UK: Britain says will work with Hong Kong leader - elect.
newsitem.headline: Britain says will work with Hong Kong leader - elect.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday sent its congratulations to Hong Kong's new leader-in-waiting and said it looked forward to working with him.

Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, 59, was the overwhelming choice on Wednesday of a 400-strong selection committee, carefully selected by Beijing, for the post of leader after the colony reverts to Chinese rule next year.

In a short statement, the British Foreign Office said: "The Prime Minister (John Major) and Foreign Secretary (Malcolm Rifkind) have sent messages of congratulations to Mr Tung, for whom there is great respect.

"British ministers have every confidence that he will be a worthy first Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. He will of course be most welcome to visit Britain at a time of his choosing."
British officials declined to expand on the statement and said it was up to Tung to decide when he wanted to visit London.
Tung declared his victory, considered a foregone conclusion in Hong Kong for weeks, a triumph for the entire Chinese nation.

But Hong Kong's pro-democracy lobby dismissed the ballot as a travesty, while liberals have expressed concern Tung would bow to Beijing's desire to curb the pace of democratic reform in the colony ruled by Britain for more than 150 years.

Britain objects to China's plan to replace Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council (Legco) on handover day with a "selected" provisional assembly, to be chosen on December 21, saying it is reprehensible and unnecessary.
But China is steaming ahead with its plans.
Foreign Office sources declined to discuss whether Tung's closeness to Beijing would affect relations with Britain.
Tung saw his fortunes almost dashed in the 1980s when the family firm ran into financial trouble but Beijing helped bail him out with a syndicated loan and he has remained close to China.
The British sources said it was now the time to "look forward", adding: "He (Tung) knows he has to win the confidence of the people he is representing."
